new.title: Tour Morges Castle and its military museum
new.desc: Château de Morges was begun around 1286 by Louis of Savoy and later housed the Bernese bailiffs from 1536 to 1798. Today it holds the Musée militaire vaudois, covering 350 years of Vaudois military history from Major Davel to General Guisan.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, with free entry on the first Sunday of the month. Check chateau-morges.ch for current hours.
new.q: Château de Morges, Rue du Château 1, Morges

new.title: Walk around Rolle Castle and the lakeside quays
new.desc: Rolle Castle on Lake Geneva was first built between 1264 and 1269 according to tree-ring dating, and passed to Bern in 1536. It is now owned by the municipality, and the courtyard and the quays beside it are open to the public.
new.tip: Only the courtyard is open, so combine it with a stroll along the quay from the marina to the beach.
new.q: Château de Rolle, Grand-Rue, Rolle

new.title: Explore Yverdon Castle and the town museum
new.desc: The Savoyard square castle of Yverdon-les-Bains was built between 1260 and 1270 for Peter of Savoy. It later housed Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi's institute, and today it is home to the Musée d'Yverdon et région with a Pestalozzi room and Egyptian antiquities.
new.tip: Open Wednesday to Sunday afternoons in most seasons; verify hours on musee-yverdon-region.ch.
new.q: Château d'Yverdon-les-Bains, Place Pestalozzi, Yverdon-les-Bains

new.title: Visit the science fiction museum Maison d'Ailleurs
new.desc: The Maison d'Ailleurs grew from the science fiction collection that Pierre Versins gave to Yverdon in 1976. It now fills a former prison built in 1806 and holds a Jules Verne collection, a spaceship mock-up and a room devoted to HR Giger.
new.tip: Allow about two hours; the documentation centre holds over 120,000 publications for researchers.
new.q: Maison d'Ailleurs, Place Pestalozzi 14, Yverdon-les-Bains

new.title: Watch automata come alive at MuMAPS in Sainte-Croix
new.desc: MuMAPS, the Musée de la mécanique d'art et du patrimoine, opened in June 2024 in Sainte-Croix by merging the CIMA, Musée Baud and Musée des Arts & Sciences. It shows the music box and automata heritage of the Jura town in two permanent exhibitions plus a yearly temporary one.
new.tip: Automata are demonstrated at set times, so check mumaps.ch for the schedule before you go.
new.q: MuMAPS, Rue de l'Industrie 2, Sainte-Croix

new.title: Look up at Lucens Castle above the Broye valley
new.desc: Lucens Castle was built from the 13th century on a rocky spur to control the Broye valley. After Bern conquered Vaud in 1536 it became a bailiff's seat, and in 1804 the canton sold it to private owners except for the chapel.
new.tip: It is privately run and mostly used for events, so call or check chateaudelucens.ch before planning an interior visit; the exterior is visible from the village.
new.q: Château de Lucens, Rue du Château, Lucens

new.title: See paper cutting at the Musée du Pays-d'Enhaut
new.desc: This village-house museum on Grand Rue in Château-d'Œx is the home of the Swiss paper-cutting centre, a craft typical of the Pays-d'Enhaut. It also shows parchments, watercolours, tools and reconstructed period rooms.
new.tip: Open afternoons, closed in part of November; admission is about CHF 12 for adults.
new.q: Musée du Vieux Pays-d'Enhaut, Grand Rue 107, Château-d'Œx

new.title: Visit the Cluniac priory church of Rougemont
new.desc: The priory of Rougemont was founded between 1073 and 1085 under the counts of Gruyère and is tied to the Payerne priory. The Église Saint-Nicolas is the main monument of the village, surrounded by old chalets with carved gables.
new.tip: The GoldenPass line between Château-d'Œx and Gstaad stops in Rougemont, a short walk from the church.
new.q: Église Saint-Nicolas, Rougemont

new.title: Admire the Grand Chalet of Rossinière, home of Balthus
new.desc: The Grand Chalet in Rossinière is one of the largest inhabitable wooden houses in Switzerland, with five floors and 113 windows. The painter Balthus bought it in 1977 and lived there until his death in 2001.
new.tip: It is private and cannot be entered, but the facade is visible from the street. Studio visits are offered only on limited dates, so check vaud.ch.
new.q: Grand Chalet, Rossinière

new.title: Visit the Audemars Piguet museum spiral in Le Brassus
new.desc: The Musée Atelier Audemars Piguet opened in June 2020 in Le Brassus. A glass spiral designed by Bjarke Ingels Group wraps around the original 1875 workshop and displays nearly 300 timepieces.
new.tip: Entry is by guided tour only and booking is required.
new.q: Musée Atelier Audemars Piguet, Route de France 18, Le Brassus

new.title: Stand in a Roman basilica at the Musée romain de Nyon
new.desc: The museum sits in the foundations of a 1st-century basilica uncovered in 1974. It presents Colonia Iulia Equestris, founded in Julius Caesar's lifetime, and its urban centre Noviodunum.
new.tip: A single ticket covers three Nyon museums, including the castle and the Musée du Léman. Children under 16 enter free.
new.q: Musée romain de Nyon, Rue Maupertuis 9, Nyon

new.title: See the Roman mosaics of Orbe-Boscéaz
new.desc: The Gallo-Roman villa of Orbe-Boscéaz was discovered in 1841 and has been excavated since 1986. Nine mosaics from the 1st to 3rd century survive in four pavilions, forming the most important group found north of the Alps, including a scene with a four-wheeled farm vehicle.
new.tip: Opening is seasonal, so check the site before you go; the villa lies about 2 km northeast of Orbe.
new.q: Mosaïques romaines d'Orbe-Boscéaz, Orbe

new.title: Discover the Musée du Cheval at La Sarraz Castle
new.desc: Switzerland's only horse museum opened in 1982 in an 18th-century barn of the La Sarraz castle. It shows horses on farms, in the army, in towns and in art, with carriages and reconstructed trades such as farriers and saddlers.
new.tip: Opening hours vary by season, mostly afternoons; the castle hosts a horse festival in August.
new.q: Musée du Cheval, Château de La Sarraz, Le Château 1, La Sarraz

new.title: Photograph the brick towers of Vufflens Castle
new.desc: Château de Vufflens was built from about 1420 to 1430 for Henri de Colombier and is a Swiss heritage site of national significance. Its tall keep is flanked by four towers and the castle is still privately owned.
new.tip: The interior is closed, but the exterior is visible from public roads; a walking loop from Morges passes it.
new.q: Château de Vufflens, Vufflens-le-Château

new.title: Follow wheat to bread at the Maison du Blé et du Pain
new.desc: This museum in Echallens occupies a building from 1790 and was inaugurated in 1989. It follows grain from field to mill to oven over four levels, and combines a museum, a working bakehouse, a restaurant and a shop.
new.tip: Hours are limited, mainly weekday mornings and afternoons; call ahead on +41 21 881 50 71.
new.q: Maison du Blé et du Pain, Place de l'Hôtel-de-Ville 5, Echallens

new.title: Descend into the Vallorbe Caves
new.desc: The Grottes de Vallorbe are the biggest caves in Switzerland, carved by the river Orbe, which sinks at the end of the Lac de Joux and reappears 4.8 km away. Entry includes the Trésor des Fées mineral museum and a light-and-sound show in the largest hall.
new.tip: Wrap up warm, as the caves are cool all year. They are mainly open from spring to autumn, with group visits in winter, so check grottesdevallorbe.ch.
new.q: Grottes de Vallorbe, Chemin de la Résurgence 1, Vallorbe

new.title: Tour the Second World War fort of Pré-Giroud
new.desc: The Pré-Giroud fort was built from 1937 to 1939 to block the Col de Jougne against any foreign army. It was bought by the commune of Vallorbe in 1988 and is now a foundation-run site with underground galleries and a museum on daily life of the troops.
new.tip: Visits are guided, with tours at 10:00, 13:00 and 15:00 in the 2026 season from May to October; see pre-giroud.ch.
new.q: Fort de Pré-Giroud, Vallorbe

new.title: Ride the mine train into the Bex salt mines
new.desc: The Mines de sel de Bex are the oldest active salt works in Switzerland, with a visit by small mine train and on foot. A longer lantern tour is also offered, and the salt is sold as Sel des Alpes.
new.tip: Book online at mines.ch; the standard visit lasts about two hours, and the bus from Bex station runs only on weekends and holidays.
new.q: Mines de sel de Bex, Route des Mines de Sel, Bex

new.title: Soak in the thermal pools of the Bains de Lavey
new.desc: The Bains de Lavey in Lavey-les-Bains use naturally hot spring water of around 62 to 69 degrees at the source, cooled to about 32 to 36 degrees in three pools. The complex includes an outdoor pool of more than 1,000 square metres, saunas and a hammam, and reopened after a renovation in late 2025.
new.tip: The sauna and hammam area is for visitors aged 16 and over, and the baths close for a short summer break, so check bains-lavey.ch.
new.q: Les Bains de Lavey, Route des Bains 48, Lavey-les-Bains

new.title: See 140,000 tulips at the Fête de la Tulipe in Morges
new.desc: The Morges tulip festival, founded in 1971, fills the Parc de l'Indépendance on the lakeshore with tens of thousands of tulips each spring. In 2026 more than 140,000 bulbs were planted, with an open-air exhibition on the history of the tulip.
new.tip: Entry to the park, quays and flower gardens is free. The festival runs from late March to around mid-May.
new.q: Parc de l'Indépendance, Morges

new.title: Hike to Mont Tendre, the roof of the Swiss Jura
new.desc: At 1,679 metres Mont Tendre is the highest summit of the Swiss Jura, inside the Parc Jura vaudois. From the top the views reach Lake Geneva, the Alps and Mont Blanc.
new.tip: The classic route from Le Sentier takes 4 to 6 hours; a shorter option follows the road from Montricher, with about 15 minutes on foot at the end.
new.q: Mont Tendre, Parc Jura vaudois, Montricher

new.title: Hike to Lac Retaud under the Diablerets glacier
new.desc: Lac Retaud is a small mountain lake that looks across to the Diablerets glacier and the peaks of Scex Rouge and Oldenhorn. A marked route links Col du Pillon with Isenau past the lake.
new.tip: Reach it from the Isenau cable car mountain station; the lake basin freezes in winter, so go in summer and early autumn.
new.q: Lac Retaud, Les Diablerets

new.title: Catch a gig at Rock Oz'Arènes in Avenches
new.desc: Rock Oz'Arènes is an August rock festival held in the Roman amphitheatre of Avenches. It is described as the smallest of the town's big summer festivals, known for an eclectic line-up with international acts.
new.tip: Tickets and dates are on rockozarenes.ch; the amphitheatre is also the setting for the Avenches Tattoo in September.
new.q: Arènes d'Avenches, Avenches

new.title: Open the Vacherin Mont-d'Or season in the Vallée de Joux
new.desc: The Fête du Vacherin Mont-d'Or in the Vallée de Joux marks the start of the season for this pine-wrapped AOP cheese, which is made from late September to April. Local dairies and ageing cellars welcome visitors during the production period, and cheesemakers wrap a strip of pine bark around each fresh cheese.
new.tip: The 2026 festival was on 26 September, from 09:00 to 18:00. Dairy visits are for booked groups through Vallée de Joux Tourisme in Le Sentier.
new.q: Vallée de Joux Tourisme, Grand-Rue 2, Le Sentier

new.title: Ride the historic BAM train through the La Côte vineyards
new.desc: The Bière-Apples-Morges metre-gauge line runs about 30 km from Morges through the vineyards and villages of the Morges hinterland to Bière. Its historic train is run as culinary outings by La Voie des Sens, including a vintners' train with stops at Chigny, Yens, Apples and Ballens.
new.tip: The heritage train runs about once a week, Thursday to Sunday, so book via myswitzerland.com or La Voie des Sens.
new.q: Gare de Morges, Place de la Gare, Morges

new.title: Taste salt-mine-aged beer at Brasserie La Mine in Bex
new.desc: The craft brewery and restaurant sits in the middle of its production site and overlooks the fermentation tanks. It offers seven fixed beers, seasonal specials and two beers aged in casks inside the Bex salt mines, with a bar and restaurant added in 2022.
new.tip: Try one of the beers aged in the mines. Hours are roughly Tuesday or Wednesday to Saturday until 23:00, and a mines and brasserie dinner package is offered.
new.q: Brasserie La Mine, Route de Massongex 4, Bex

new.title: Eat perch fillets with chive sauce at the Restaurant des Quais
new.desc: This lakeside restaurant in Grandson is known across French-speaking Switzerland for its perch fillets with chive sauce. It stands on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel below Grandson Castle.
new.tip: Order the filets de perche sauce à la ciboulette. Check the address and opening days locally, as listings differ slightly.
new.q: Restaurant des Quais, Chemin du Lac 43, Grandson

new.title: Eat moitié-moitié fondue at Le Chalet in Château-d'Œx
new.desc: Le Chalet in Château-d'Œx is both a restaurant and a demonstration cheese dairy. Time Out describes a classic Vaudois half-and-half fondue of Chalet and L'Etivaz cheeses.
new.tip: Cheesemaking is shown free on Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays from 11:00 to 13:00, May to October. It is a short walk from the station.
new.q: Le Chalet restaurant et fromagerie de démonstration, Route de la Gare 2, Château-d'Œx

new.title: Order perch fillets at Au Vieux Navire in Buchillon
new.desc: Au Vieux Navire in Buchillon, a short drive from Morges, is known for its perch fillets. They come with lemon, with tomato or in a champagne homardine sauce, and the restaurant is recognised by GaultMillau.
new.tip: Pair the perch with a local La Côte Chasselas.
new.q: Restaurant Au Vieux Navire, Buchillon

new.title: Eat baked Vacherin Mont-d'Or at the Refuge de Solalex
new.desc: The Refuge de Solalex is a mountain restaurant in the Gryon area with regional dishes, log-fire raclette, fondue, forest mushroom feuilletés and baked Vacherin Mont-d'Or.
new.tip: It is open daily from early May to mid-November and from mid-December to early April, so check before you go.
new.q: Refuge de Solalex, Solalex, Gryon

new.title: Lunch in the revolving Kuklos restaurant above Leysin
new.desc: Le Kuklos is a round glass revolving restaurant on La Berneuse at 2,048 metres, echoing the neighbouring peaks Tour de Mayen and Tour d'Aï. It turns once every hour and a half with views of the Eiger north face and Mont Blanc, and serves cheese dishes, rösti and regional specialities.
new.tip: Take the Aigle-Leysin cog railway and then the Berneuse gondola. It is open in summer, from mid-June to mid-October.
new.q: Restaurant tournant Le Kuklos, La Berneuse, Leysin

new.title: Try the Malakoff cheese fritter at the Auberge communale de Gilly
new.desc: The Auberge communale de Gilly, in the La Côte vineyards, highlights the Malakoff, a local fried cheese specialty. The dish is a staple of Vaud village inns.
new.tip: Order the Malakoff, ideally with a glass of La Côte white. Check opening days before driving out.
new.q: Auberge communale de Gilly, Gilly

new.title: Taste Chasselas at Domaine du Martheray in Féchy
new.desc: Domaine du Martheray farms about 15 hectares of vines in Féchy on La Côte, planted with Chasselas and Chardonnay. Its Grand Cru and Premier Grand Cru wines are rated in the high 80s to low 90s by Falstaff.
new.tip: Tastings are by appointment and cost roughly CHF 20 to 30. Pair it with the Balade des Capites trail through the Féchy vineyards.
new.q: Domaine du Martheray, Féchy

new.title: Eat a fondue or croûte at the Chalet du Crêt Blanc
new.desc: The Chalet du Crêt Blanc is a mountain restaurant above Le Pont in the Vallée de Joux. Its menu includes croûtes, rösti, fondue and salads.
new.tip: It is seasonal and closed on Mondays, so check opening dates before hiking up.
new.q: Chalet du Crêt Blanc, Le Pont
